Taking the downward direction as positive, the radius of the first surface is $R_1 = -60$ cm and the radius of the second surface is $R_2 = -20$ cm.

The power of the glass lens is given by:
$P_g = (\mu_g - 1) \left( $\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)
$P_g = (1.5 - 1) \left( $\dfrac{1}{-60} - \dfrac{1}{-20} \right) =$0.5 \left( $\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{60} \right) = \dfrac{1}{60} \text{ cm}^{-1}

The bottom surface is silvered and acts as a mirror for light traveling inside the glass. Its radius of curvature is $R_2 = -20$ cm.
Power of the equivalent mirror:
$P_m = $-\dfrac{2}{R_2} = -\dfrac{2}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{10} \text{ cm}^{-1}

The equivalent power of the initial system is:
$P = 2P_g + P_m = 2 \left( $\dfrac{1}{60} \right) + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{4}{30} = \dfrac{2}{15} \text{ cm}^{-1}

The equivalent focal length is $F = $\dfrac{15}{2} =$7.5$ cm. For the image to coincide with the pin, the pin must be at the center of curvature of the equivalent mirror.
Initial position $u_1 = 2F = 15$ cm.

When water is filled in the concave section, a plano-convex water lens is formed with $R_{w1} = \infty$ and $R_{w2} = -60$ cm.
Power of the water lens:
$P_w = (\mu_w - 1) \left( $\dfrac{1}{R_{w1}} - \dfrac{1}{R_{w2}} \right) = \left( \dfrac{4}{3} -$1 \right) \left( 0 - $\dfrac{1}{-60} \right) = \dfrac{1}{180} \text{ cm}^{-1}

The new equivalent power of the system is:
$P' = 2P_w + P = 2 \left( $\dfrac{1}{180} \right) + \dfrac{2}{15} = \dfrac{1}{90} + \dfrac{12}{90} = \dfrac{13}{90} \text{ cm}^{-1}

The new equivalent focal length is $F' = $\dfrac{90}{13} cm.
New position for the image to coincide is $u_2 = 2F' = $\dfrac{180}{13} \approx$13.85$ cm.

Distance the pin must be moved is:
$\Delta u = u_1 - u_2 = 15 - $\dfrac{180}{13} = \dfrac{15}{13} \approx$1.15 \text{ cm}$

Since $u_2 < u_1$, the pin must be moved towards the lens. The closest matching option provided is $1.14 \text{ cm}$ towards the lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A double convex lens has a focal length of $25 \text{ cm}$. The radius of curvature of one of its surfaces is twice that of the other. Determine the radii, given that the refractive index of the lens material is $1.5$.
questions.solution:
Given $f = 25 \text{ cm}$ and $\mu = 1.5$.

Let the radii of curvature of the double convex lens be $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = -2R$.

Using the lens maker's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)

Substituting the given values:

\dfrac{1}{25} = ($1.5 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-2R} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{25} = 0.5 \left( $\dfrac{1}{R} + \dfrac{1}{2R} \right)

\dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left( \dfrac{3}{2R} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{3}{4R}$

$4R = 75 \Rightarrow R = 18.75 $\text{ cm}

The other radius is $2R = 2 \times18.75 = 37.5 $\text{ cm}.

The radii of curvature are $18.75 $\text{ cm}and $37.5 $\text{ cm}.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lens has radii of curvature of $+20 \text{ cm}$ and $+30 \text{ cm}$. The material of the lens has a refracting index of $1.6$. Determine the focal length of the lens when it is placed in air.
questions.solution:
Using the Lens Maker's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) $\$left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)

Given $R_1 = +20 \text{ cm}$, $R_2 = +30 \text{ cm}$, and $\mu = 1.6$.

Substituting the values:

\dfrac{1}{f} = ($1.6 - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.6 \times $\$left(\dfrac{3 - 2}{60}\right)

\dfrac{1}{f} =$0.6 \times $\dfrac{1}{60}

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{100}

$f = +100 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radii of curvature of a lens are $+20 \text{ cm}$ and $+30 \text{ cm}$. The refracting index of the lens material is $1.6$. Find the focal length of the lens if it is placed in water ($\mu = 1.33$).
questions.solution:
Using the lens maker's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \left( $\dfrac{\mu_l}{\mu_m} -$1 \right) \left( $\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)

Given $\mu_l = 1.6$, $\mu_m = 1.33 \approx $\dfrac{4}{3}, $R_1 = +20 \text{ cm}$, and $R_2 = +30 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting the values:

\dfrac{1}{f} = \left( \dfrac{1.6}{4/3} - 1 \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \left( $\dfrac{4.8}{4} -$1 \right) \left( $\dfrac{3 - 2}{60} \right)

\dfrac{1}{f} = ($1.2 - 1) \times $\dfrac{1}{60}

\dfrac{1}{f} =$0.2 \times $\dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{1}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{60}

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{300}

$f = 300 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Lenses are fabricated from a material having a refractive index of $1.50$. The magnitudes of the radii of curvature are $20 \text{ cm}$ and $30 \text{ cm}$. Determine the focal lengths of all the possible lenses that can be formed with these specifications.
questions.solution:
Using the lens maker's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( $\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)

Given $\mu = 1.50$, the term $(\mu - 1) = 0.5 = $\dfrac{1}{2}. The magnitudes of the radii of curvature are $20 \text{ cm}$ and $30 \text{ cm}$.

Depending on the type of lens (biconvex, biconcave, concavo-convex, or convexo-concave), the signs of $R_1$ and $R_2$ can be positive or negative. The possible values for the term \left( $\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right) are:

Case 1: $R_1$ and $R_2$ have opposite signs.

\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} = \pm \left( \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{30} \right) = \pm \left( \dfrac{3 + 2}{60} \right) = \pm \dfrac{1}{12} \text{ cm}^{-1}

Substituting into the formula:

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \pm \dfrac{1}{12} \right) = \pm \dfrac{1}{24} \text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow$f = \pm 24 \text{ cm}$

Case 2: $R_1$ and $R_2$ have the same sign.

\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} = \pm \left( \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} \right) = \pm \left( \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} \right) = \pm \dfrac{1}{60} \text{ cm}^{-1}

Substituting into the formula:

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \pm \dfrac{1}{60} \right) = \pm \dfrac{1}{120} \text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow$f = \pm 120 \text{ cm}$

Therefore, the possible focal lengths are $\pm 24 \text{ cm}$ and $\pm 120 \text{ cm}$.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin biconvex lens, constructed from a material with refractive index $\mu_2$, is flanked by a medium of refractive index $\mu_1$ on one side and a medium of refractive index $\mu_3$ on the opposite side. Both radii of curvature of the lens have the same magnitude $R$. A beam of light travelling parallel to the principal axis is incident on the lens from the medium $\mu_1$. Determine the position where the image will be formed.
questions.solution:
Applying the formula for refraction at a spherical surface for the first surface:

$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} - \dfrac{\mu_1}{u} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R_1}$

Given that the incident beam is parallel to the principal axis, $u = -\infty$. For a biconvex lens, $R_1 = +R$.

$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$

For the second surface, the image formed by the first surface acts as a virtual object.

$\dfrac{\mu_3}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_3 - \mu_2}{R_2}$

For the biconvex lens, $R_2 = -R$.

$\dfrac{\mu_3}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_3 - \mu_2}{-R} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_3}{R}$

Adding the equations for both surfaces:

$\dfrac{\mu_3}{v} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R} + \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_3}{R}$

$\dfrac{\mu_3}{v} = \dfrac{2\mu_2 - \mu_1 - \mu_3}{R}$

$v = \dfrac{\mu_3 R}{2\mu_2 - \mu_1 - \mu_3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A biconvex thin lens, fabricated from a material of refractive index $\mu_2$, separates a medium of refractive index $\mu_1$ on one face and a medium of refractive index $\mu_3$ on the other face. The two radii of curvature of the lens share an equal magnitude $R$. A beam of light travelling parallel to the principal axis strikes the lens from the medium $\mu_3$. At what position will the image be formed?
questions.solution:
For the first refraction at the surface separating medium $\mu_3$ and the lens $\mu_2$, the incident light is parallel to the principal axis, so the object is at infinity ($u = -\infty$). The radius of curvature for the first biconvex surface is $R_1 = +R$.

Using the formula for refraction at a spherical surface:

$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} - \dfrac{\mu_3}{-\infty} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_3}{R}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_3}{R}$

For the second refraction at the surface separating the lens $\mu_2$ and medium $\mu_1$, the image formed by the first surface acts as a virtual object. The radius of curvature for the second biconvex surface is $R_2 = -R$.

$\dfrac{\mu_1}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_1 - \mu_2}{-R}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\mu_1}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_2}{v_1} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$

Adding the two equations to eliminate $v_1$, we get:

$\dfrac{\mu_1}{v} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_3}{R} + \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\mu_1}{v} = \dfrac{2\mu_2 - \mu_1 - \mu_3}{R}$

$\Rightarrow v = \dfrac{\mu_1 R}{2\mu_2 - \mu_1 - \mu_3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens has a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$. Determine the location and nature of the image when a point object is positioned on the principal axis at a distance of $9.8 \text{ cm}$ from the lens.
options: $510 \text{ cm}$ on the side of the object, virtual
$510 \text{ cm}$ on the other side, real
$490 \text{ cm}$ on the other side, real
$490 \text{ cm}$ on the side of the object, virtual
questions.solution:
Given $f = +10 \text{ cm}$ and $u = -9.8 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{9.8}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{10}{98}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{49 - 50}{490}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{490}$

$v = -490 \text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the image is formed on the same side as the object. Since the image is formed by actual divergence of rays from the same side, it is virtual.

Therefore, the image is at $490 \text{ cm}$ on the side of the object and is virtual.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens has a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$. Determine the location and nature of the image when a point object is positioned on the principal axis at a distance of $10.2 \text{ cm}$ from the lens.
options: $510 \text{ cm}$ on the side of the object, virtual
$490 \text{ cm}$ on the side of the object, virtual
$490 \text{ cm}$ on the other side, real
$510 \text{ cm}$ on the other side, real
questions.solution:
Given focal length of the convex lens, $f = +10 \text{ cm}$

Object distance, $u = -10.2 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-10.2} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{10.2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{10.2 - 10}{10 \times 10.2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{0.2}{102} = \dfrac{1}{510}$

$v = +510 \text{ cm}$

Since $v$ is positive, the image is real and formed at a distance of $510 \text{ cm}$ on the other side of the lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A slide projector is required to project a $35 \text{ mm}$ slide ($35 \text{ mm} \times 23 \text{ mm}$) onto a $2 \text{ m} \times 2 \text{ m}$ screen located at a distance of $10 \text{ m}$ from the lens. Determine the focal length of the projector's lens.
questions.solution:
To project the entire slide onto the screen, the maximum magnification is determined by fitting the larger dimension of the slide ($35 \text{ mm}$) onto the screen ($2 \text{ m}$).

Magnification $m = \dfrac{v}{|u|} = \dfrac{2000 \text{ mm}}{35 \text{ mm}} = \dfrac{400}{7}$

Given the image distance $v = 10 \text{ m} = 1000 \text{ cm}$, the object distance $|u|$ is:

$|u| = \dfrac{v}{m} = \dfrac{1000}{\dfrac{400}{7}} = 17.5 \text{ cm}$

Using the sign convention, $u = -17.5 \text{ cm}$ and $v = +1000 \text{ cm}$. Applying the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{1000} - $\$left(-\dfrac{1}{17.5}\right)

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{1000} + \dfrac{1}{17.5} = \dfrac{17.5 + 1000}{17500} = \dfrac{1017.5}{17500}

$f = $\dfrac{17500}{1017.5} \approx$17.2 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Along the principal axis of a convex lens having a focal length of $12 \text{ cm}$, a particle performs simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $1.0 \text{ cm}$. The oscillation has its mean position located $20 \text{ cm}$ away from the lens. Determine the amplitude of oscillation for the particle's image.
questions.solution:
Given the focal length of the convex lens, $f = +12 \text{ cm}$.

The mean position of the particle is at $u = -20 \text{ cm}$ and its amplitude of oscillation is $A_o = 1.0 \text{ cm}$.

The extreme positions of the oscillating particle on the principal axis are $u_1 = -20 - 1 = -21 \text{ cm}$ and $u_2 = -20 + 1 = -19 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula, $v = \dfrac{uf}{u+f}$, we find the corresponding extreme positions of the image.

For $u_1 = -21 \text{ cm}$:
$v_1 = \dfrac{-21 \times 12}{-21 + 12} = \dfrac{-252}{-9} = 28 \text{ cm}$

For $u_2 = -19 \text{ cm}$:
$v_2 = \dfrac{-19 \times 12}{-19 + 12} = \dfrac{-228}{-7} = \dfrac{228}{7} \text{ cm}$

The path length of the image's oscillation is the distance between these two extreme positions:
Path length $= v_2 - v_1 = \dfrac{228}{7} - 28 = \dfrac{228 - 196}{7} = \dfrac{32}{7} \text{ cm}$

The amplitude of oscillation for the image is half of its path length:
$A_i = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{32}{7} = \dfrac{16}{7} \approx 2.28 \text{ cm} \approx 2.3 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An extended object is placed at a distance of $5.0 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $8.0 \text{ cm}$. If a ray diagram is drawn to scale to locate the image, what is the distance of the image from the lens measured from this diagram?
questions.solution:
Given object distance, $u = -5.0 \text{ cm}$

Focal length of the convex lens, $f = +8.0 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{8.0} + \dfrac{1}{-5.0}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{5 - 8}{40} = -\dfrac{3}{40}$

$v = -\dfrac{40}{3} \approx -13.3 \text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that a virtual image is formed on the same side as the object. The distance of the image from the lens is $13.3 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An extended object is placed at a distance of $5.0 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $8.0 \text{ cm}$. Find the position of the image from the lens formula, applying the standard Cartesian sign convention (with the object placed at $u = -5.0 \text{ cm}$).
questions.solution:
Given the object distance $u = -5.0 \text{ cm}$ and the focal length of the convex lens $f = +8.0 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-5.0} = \dfrac{1}{8.0}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{5.0} = \dfrac{1}{8.0}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{8.0} - \dfrac{1}{5.0}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{5 - 8}{40} = -\dfrac{3}{40}$

$v = -\dfrac{40}{3} \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pin of length $2.00 \text{ cm}$ is positioned perpendicular to the principal axis of a converging lens. An inverted image measuring $1.00 \text{ cm}$ in size is produced at a distance of $40.0 \text{ cm}$ from the pin. Determine the focal length of the lens and its distance from the pin.
questions.solution:
Given height of the object, $h_o = 2.00 \text{ cm}$

Height of the inverted image, $h_i = -1.00 \text{ cm}$

Distance between the object and the image, $D = 40.0 \text{ cm}$

Magnification of the lens is given by $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{h_i}{h_o}$

$\dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-1.00}{2.00} = -0.5 \Rightarrow v = -0.5u$

For a real image, the object and image are on opposite sides of the lens. The distance between them is $v - u = 40.0 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting $v = -0.5u$:

$-0.5u - u = 40.0$

$-1.5u = 40.0 \Rightarrow u = -\dfrac{80}{3} \approx -26.7 \text{ cm}$

The distance of the lens from the pin is $|u| = 26.7 \text{ cm}$.

The image distance is $v = -0.5 \times \left(-\dfrac{80}{3}\right) = \dfrac{40}{3} \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{3}{40} - $\$left(-\dfrac{3}{80}\right)

\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{6}{80} + \dfrac{3}{80} = \dfrac{9}{80}

$f = $\dfrac{80}{9} \approx$8.89 \text{ cm}$

The focal length of the lens is $8.89 \text{ cm}$ and its distance from the pin is $26.7 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A double size real image is produced by a convex lens when an object is placed $18 \text{ cm}$ away from it. To produce a triple size real image, where should the object be placed?
questions.solution:
For a convex lens, the magnification $m$ in terms of focal length $f$ and object distance $u$ is given by $m = \dfrac{f}{f + u}$.

For a real image, the magnification is negative.

In the first case, a double size real image is formed when the object is placed $18 \text{ cm}$ away.

$m_1 = -2$ and $u_1 = -18 \text{ cm}$.

$-2 = \dfrac{f}{f - 18}$

$-2f + 36 = f$

$3f = 36 \Rightarrow f = 12 \text{ cm}$

In the second case, a triple size real image is required.

$m_2 = -3$

$-3 = \dfrac{12}{12 + u_2}$

$-36 - 3u_2 = 12$

$-3u_2 = 48 \Rightarrow u_2 = -16 \text{ cm}$

The object should be placed $16 \text{ cm}$ away from the lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pin of length $2.0 \text{ cm}$ lies along the principal axis of a converging lens, with its centre positioned at a distance of $11 \text{ cm}$ from the lens. The lens has a focal length of $6 \text{ cm}$. Determine the size of the image.
questions.solution:
Given:
Length of the pin, $L_o = 2.0 \text{ cm}$
Focal length of the converging lens, $f = +6 \text{ cm}$
Distance of the centre of the pin from the lens $= 11 \text{ cm}$

Since the pin lies along the principal axis, its ends are located at distances of $11 - 1 = 10 \text{ cm}$ and $11 + 1 = 12 \text{ cm}$ from the optical centre of the lens.
Thus, the object coordinates for the two ends are $u_1 = -10 \text{ cm}$ and $u_2 = -12 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{uf}{u+f}$

For the first end ($u_1 = -10 \text{ cm}$):
$v_1 = \dfrac{-10 \times 6}{-10 + 6} = \dfrac{-60}{-4} = 15 \text{ cm}$

For the second end ($u_2 = -12 \text{ cm}$):
$v_2 = \dfrac{-12 \times 6}{-12 + 6} = \dfrac{-72}{-6} = 12 \text{ cm}$

The size of the image is the distance between the images of the two ends:
$L_i = |v_2 - v_1| = |12 - 15| = 3 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance of the sun from the earth is $1.5 \times 10^{11} \text{ m}$, and its diameter is $1.4 \times 10^9 \text{ m}$. Determine the radius of the sun's image produced by a lens with a focal length of $20 \text{ cm}$.
questions.solution:
The angle subtended by the sun at the optical centre of the lens is given by $\alpha = \dfrac{D}{u}$, where $D$ is the diameter of the sun and $u$ is the distance of the sun from the earth.

Since the sun is at a very large distance, its image is formed at the focal plane of the lens. The angle subtended by the image at the optical centre is equal to the angle subtended by the sun.

The diameter of the image $d$ is given by $d = f \alpha = \dfrac{f D}{u}$, where $f$ is the focal length of the lens.

The radius of the image is $r = \dfrac{d}{2} = \dfrac{f D}{2 u}$.

Substituting the given values, $f = 0.2 \text{ m}$, $D = 1.4 \times 10^9 \text{ m}$, and $u = 1.5 \times 10^{11} \text{ m}$:

$r = \dfrac{0.2 \times 1.4 \times 10^9}{2 \times 1.5 \times 10^{11}}$

$r = \dfrac{0.28 \times 10^9}{3.0 \times 10^{11}} \text{ m}$

$r = \dfrac{0.28}{300} \text{ m} = \dfrac{280}{300} \text{ mm}$

$r = \dfrac{14}{15} \text{ mm} \approx 0.933 \text{ mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $5.0$ diopter lens produces a virtual image which is $4$ times the object placed perpendicularly on the principal axis of the lens. Determine the distance of the object from the lens.
questions.solution:
Power of the lens, $P = 5.0 \text{ D}$

Focal length, $f = \dfrac{100}{P} = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20 \text{ cm}$

Since the lens forms a virtual and magnified image, the magnification is $m = +4$.

Using the relation $m = \dfrac{v}{u}$, we get $v = 4u$.

Applying the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{4u} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1 - 4}{4u} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{-3}{4u} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$4u = -60 \Rightarrow u = -15 \text{ cm}$

The distance of the object from the lens is $15 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diverging lens with a focal length of $20 \text{ cm}$ and a converging mirror with a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$ are arranged coaxially with a separation of $5 \text{ cm}$. At what distance should an object be placed such that a real image is formed at the location of the object itself?
options: $20 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror
$30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror
$60 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror
$40 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror
questions.solution:
For the final image to form at the location of the object itself, the light rays must retrace their path after reflection from the mirror.

This condition is satisfied if the rays from the lens strike the mirror normally, which requires the image formed by the lens to be at the center of curvature of the mirror.

The focal length of the converging mirror is $f_M = 10 \text{ cm}$, so its radius of curvature is $R = 20 \text{ cm}$. The center of curvature is $20 \text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror.

Since the distance between the lens and the mirror is $5 \text{ cm}$, the center of curvature is located $20 - 5 = 15 \text{ cm}$ in front of the lens.

The diverging lens must form a virtual image of the object at this position, so the image distance for the lens is $v = -15 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f_L}$ with $f_L = -20 \text{ cm}$:

$\dfrac{1}{-15} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{3 - 4}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$

$u = -60 \text{ cm}$

The object should be placed $60 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror.

Answer: $60 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side further away from the mirror

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens of focal length $12 \text{ cm}$ and a diverging mirror of focal length $7.5 \text{ cm}$ are positioned $5.0 \text{ cm}$ apart with their principal axes coinciding. Determine where an object should be placed so that its image falls on itself.
options: $15 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, further away from the mirror
$30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, further away from the mirror
$7.5 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, further away from the mirror
$60 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, further away from the mirror
questions.solution:
For the final image to coincide with the object, the light rays must retrace their path after reflection from the diverging (convex) mirror.

This is possible only if the rays refracted by the convex lens fall normally on the convex mirror. For a convex mirror, rays fall normally if they are directed towards its center of curvature.

The radius of curvature of the convex mirror is $R = 2f = 2 \times 7.5 = 15 \text{ cm}$.

Thus, the image formed by the lens must be at the center of curvature of the mirror, which is $15 \text{ cm}$ behind the mirror.

The distance of this image from the lens is $v = 5.0 + 15 = 20 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$:

$\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{3 - 5}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{30}$

$u = -30 \text{ cm}$

The object should be placed $30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, further away from the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens and a diverging mirror are positioned with a separation of $15 \text{ cm}$. The focal length of the lens is $25 \text{ cm}$ while that of the mirror is $40 \text{ cm}$. Determine where a point source must be placed between the lens and the mirror so that the light, following reflection by the mirror and subsequent transmission through the lens, emerges parallel to the principal axis.
questions.solution:
For the light to emerge parallel to the principal axis after passing through the converging lens, the virtual object for the lens (which is the image formed by the mirror) must lie at the focal point of the lens.

Since the light travels from the mirror to the lens, the focal point of the lens for this incident light is at a distance of $25 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, on the side of the mirror.

The separation between the lens and the mirror is $15 \text{ cm}$. Therefore, the image formed by the mirror must be located $25 - 15 = 10 \text{ cm}$ behind the mirror.

For the diverging (convex) mirror, the focal length is $f = +40 \text{ cm}$ and the image distance is $v = +10 \text{ cm}$.

Using the mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{40}$

$\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1 - 4}{40} = -\dfrac{3}{40}$

$u = -\dfrac{40}{3} \approx -13.33 \text{ cm}$

The point source must be placed at a distance of $13.33 \text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror.

The distance of the point source from the lens is:

$15 - 13.33 = 1.67 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens with a focal length of $15 \text{ cm}$ and a converging mirror with a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$ are positioned $50 \text{ cm}$ apart, sharing a common principal axis. A point source is situated between the lens and the mirror, at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ from the lens. Determine the locations of the two images formed.
options: $24 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror, and $15 \text{ cm}$ from the lens away from the mirror
$15 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror, and $24 \text{ cm}$ from the lens away from the mirror
$15 \text{ cm}$ and $24 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, both on the side away from the mirror
$10 \text{ cm}$ and $30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, both on the side away from the mirror
questions.solution:
The light from the point source can form an image in two ways: by directly refracting through the lens, and by first reflecting from the mirror and then refracting through the lens.

For the first image (formed directly by the lens):
The source is at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ from the lens.
Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{1}{15}$
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{8 - 3}{120} = \dfrac{1}{24}$
$v_1 = +24 \text{ cm}$
The positive sign indicates that the image is formed on the side opposite to the object, which is away from the mirror.

For the second image (formed after reflection from the mirror):
The distance between the lens and the mirror is $50 \text{ cm}$. The source is $40 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, so it is $50 - 40 = 10 \text{ cm}$ from the mirror.
For the converging (concave) mirror, $u_m = -10 \text{ cm}$ and $f_m = -10 \text{ cm}$.
Using the mirror formula $\dfrac{1}{v_m} + \dfrac{1}{u_m} = \dfrac{1}{f_m}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_m} - \dfrac{1}{10} = -\dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_m} = 0 \Rightarrow v_m = \infty$
The reflected rays become parallel to the principal axis and travel towards the lens.
For the lens, these parallel rays act as an object at infinity ($u_2 = -\infty$).
Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-\infty} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow v_2 = +15 \text{ cm}$
Since the rays are coming from the mirror, they pass through the lens and converge on the other side, which is away from the mirror.

Thus, the two images are formed at $15 \text{ cm}$ and $24 \text{ cm}$ from the lens, both on the side away from the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens having a focal length of $15 \text{ cm}$ and a converging mirror with a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$ are positioned $50 \text{ cm}$ apart along a common principal axis. At what location on the principal axis must a point source be situated such that the two images are formed at the identical position?
options: $25 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror
$20 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror
$15 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror
$30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror
questions.solution:
Let the point source be placed at a distance $x$ from the lens.

The distance of the point source from the mirror is $50 - x$.

Two images are formed by the optical system for an observer looking through the lens: one by the direct refraction of light through the lens, and another by the reflection of light from the mirror followed by refraction through the lens.

For these two final images to form at the identical position, the light in both paths must act as identical objects for the lens. This means the intermediate image formed by the mirror must coincide exactly with the position of the point source.

A converging mirror forms an image at the object's location when the object is placed at its center of curvature.

The radius of curvature of the mirror is $R = 2f = 2 \times 10 = 20$ cm.

Thus, the point source must be placed at a distance of $20$ cm from the mirror.

The location of the point source from the lens is $50 - 20 = 30$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens of focal length $15 \text{ cm}$ and a converging mirror of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$ are positioned $50 \text{ cm}$ apart. A pin of length $2.0 \text{ cm}$ is kept $30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side farther from the mirror. Determine the position and the size of the final image.
options: At the object itself, of size $4.0 \text{ cm}$
$10 \text{ cm}$ from the mirror, of size $1.0 \text{ cm}$
$30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens towards the mirror, of size $2.0 \text{ cm}$
At the object itself, of size $2.0 \text{ cm}$
questions.solution:
For the first refraction through the converging lens:

Object distance, $u_1 = -30 \text{ cm}$

Focal length, $f_1 = +15 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow v_1 = +30 \text{ cm}$

Magnification, $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{30}{-30} = -1$

The first image is formed $30 \text{ cm}$ to the right of the lens.

For the reflection from the converging (concave) mirror:

Distance between the lens and the mirror is $50 \text{ cm}$.

Object distance for the mirror, $u_2 = -(50 - 30) = -20 \text{ cm}$

Focal length of the mirror, $f_2 = -10 \text{ cm}$

Using the mirror formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} + \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} + \dfrac{1}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{-10} \Rightarrow v_2 = -20 \text{ cm}$

Magnification, $m_2 = -\dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = -\dfrac{-20}{-20} = -1$

The second image is formed $20 \text{ cm}$ in front of the mirror, which is $30 \text{ cm}$ to the right of the lens. This coincides with the center of curvature of the mirror, so the rays retrace their path.

For the second refraction through the lens:

The light rays travel back towards the lens.

Object distance for the lens, $u_3 = -30 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_3} - \dfrac{1}{u_3} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_3} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15} \Rightarrow v_3 = +30 \text{ cm}$

The final image is formed $30 \text{ cm}$ to the left of the lens, which is exactly at the original object position.

Magnification, $m_3 = \dfrac{v_3}{u_3} = \dfrac{30}{-30} = -1$

Total magnification, $m = m_1 \times m_2 \times m_3 = (-1) \times (-1) \times (-1) = -1$

Size of the final image $= |m| \times h_o = 1 \times 2.0 \text{ cm} = 2.0 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point object is situated on the principal axis of a convex lens ($f = 15 \text{ cm}$) at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ from it. On the opposite side of the lens, a glass plate ($\mu = 1.50$) of thickness $1 \text{ cm}$ is positioned perpendicular to the axis. Determine the distance of the final image of the point object from the lens.
questions.solution:
For the convex lens, the object distance is $u = -30 \text{ cm}$ and the focal length is $f = +15 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$

$v = 30 \text{ cm}$

The lens forms an image at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ on the opposite side.

When a glass plate is placed in the path of the converging rays, it produces a shift in the position of the image in the direction of the incident light. The shift is given by:

$\Delta x = t \left(1 - $\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)

Substituting $t = 1 \text{ cm}$ and $\mu = 1.5 = $\dfrac{3}{2}:

$\Delta x = 1 \left(1 - $\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3} \text{ cm} \approx$0.33 \text{ cm}$

Since the shift is in the direction of the incident light (away from the lens), the distance of the final image from the lens is:

$v' = v + \Delta x = 30 + 0.33 = 30.33 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $20 \text{ cm}$ and a concave lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$ are placed $10 \text{ cm}$ apart with their principal axes coinciding. A beam of light travelling parallel to the principal axis and having a beam diameter of $5.0 \text{ mm}$, is incident on the combination. The emergent beam is parallel to the incident one. Find the possible values for the beam diameter of the emergent beam.
questions.solution:
Case I: Light is incident on the convex lens first.

The incident parallel beam converges towards the principal focus of the convex lens, which is at a distance of $20 \text{ cm}$ from it.

The concave lens is placed $10 \text{ cm}$ from the convex lens. The distance of the focus of the convex lens from the concave lens is $20 - 10 = 10 \text{ cm}$.

This point acts as a virtual object for the concave lens. Since the focal length of the concave lens is $10 \text{ cm}$, the emergent beam becomes parallel to the principal axis.

Using similar triangles, the diameter of the emergent beam $D_2$ is related to the incident beam diameter $D_1$ by:

$\dfrac{D_2}{D_1} = \dfrac{10}{20}$

$D_2 = 5.0 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 2.5 \text{ mm}$

Case II: Light is incident on the concave lens first.

The incident parallel beam diverges from the principal focus of the concave lens, which is at a distance of $10 \text{ cm}$ in front of it.

The convex lens is placed $10 \text{ cm}$ behind the concave lens. The distance of the focus of the concave lens from the convex lens is $10 + 10 = 20 \text{ cm}$.

This point acts as a real object for the convex lens. Since the focal length of the convex lens is $20 \text{ cm}$, the emergent beam becomes parallel to the principal axis.

Using similar triangles, the diameter of the emergent beam $D_2$ is related to the incident beam diameter $D_1$ by:

$\dfrac{D_2}{D_1} = \dfrac{20}{10}$

$D_2 = 5.0 \times 2 = 10.0 \text{ mm} = 1.0 \text{ cm}$

Therefore, the possible values for the beam diameter of the emergent beam are $2.5 \text{ mm}$ and $1.0 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diverging lens having a focal length of $20 ext{ cm}$ and a converging lens having a focal length of $30 ext{ cm}$ are positioned $15 ext{ cm}$ apart, with their principal axes coinciding. Where must an object be situated on the principal axis in order for its final image to be formed at infinity?
options: $150 ext{ cm}$ from the converging lens
$30 ext{ cm}$ from the diverging lens
$60 ext{ cm}$ from the diverging lens
$210 ext{ cm}$ from the converging lens
questions.solution:
Considering the case where light passes through the diverging lens first, then the converging lens.

For the final image to be at infinity, the image formed by the diverging lens must lie at the first principal focus of the converging lens.

The focal length of the converging lens is $f_2 = +30 \text{ cm}$.

The focus of the converging lens is $30 \text{ cm}$ in front of it. Since the diverging lens is placed $15 \text{ cm}$ in front of the converging lens, the image formed by the diverging lens must be at $30 - 15 = 15 \text{ cm}$ in front of the diverging lens.

For the diverging lens, $v_1 = -15 \text{ cm}$ and $f_1 = -20 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{-15} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 4}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$

$u_1 = -60 \text{ cm}$

The object must be placed $60 \text{ cm}$ from the diverging lens.

Considering the case where light passes through the converging lens first, then the diverging lens.

For the final image to be at infinity, the image formed by the converging lens must act as a virtual object at the focus of the diverging lens.

The focal length of the diverging lens is $f_2 = -20 \text{ cm}$.

The focus is $20 \text{ cm}$ behind the diverging lens. Since the diverging lens is $15 \text{ cm}$ behind the converging lens, the image formed by the converging lens must be at $15 + 20 = 35 \text{ cm}$ behind the converging lens.

For the converging lens, $v_1 = +35 \text{ cm}$ and $f_1 = +30 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{35} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{30}$

$\dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{35} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{6 - 7}{210} = -\dfrac{1}{210}$

$u_1 = -210 \text{ cm}$

The object must be placed $210 \text{ cm}$ from the converging lens.

Answer: $60 ext{ cm}$ from the diverging lens; $210 ext{ cm}$ from the converging lens

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Situated at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$ is a $5 \text{ mm}$ high pin. A second lens having a focal length of $5 \text{ cm}$ is positioned $40 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens and $55 \text{ cm}$ from the pin. Determine the position of the final image.
options: $5 \text{ cm}$ from the second lens, further away
$10 \text{ cm}$ from the second lens, further away
$10 \text{ cm}$ from the second lens, towards the first lens
$20 \text{ cm}$ from the second lens, further away
questions.solution:
For the first lens:

$u_1 = -15 \text{ cm}$, $f_1 = 10 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30}$

$v_1 = 30 \text{ cm}$

The image formed by the first lens acts as an object for the second lens. The distance between the lenses is $40 \text{ cm}$.

Object distance for the second lens, $u_2 = -(40 - 30) = -10 \text{ cm}$

Focal length of the second lens, $f_2 = 5 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula again, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$v_2 = 10 \text{ cm}$

The positive sign indicates that the final image is formed $10 \text{ cm}$ from the second lens on the side opposite to the object, which is further away from the first lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $5 \text{ mm}$ high pin is situated at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$. Positioned $40 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens and $55 \text{ cm}$ from the pin is a second lens having a focal length of $5 \text{ cm}$. Identify the nature of the final image.
questions.solution:
For the first lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v_1 = 30 \text{ cm}$

Magnification of the first lens, $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2$

The image formed by the first lens acts as the object for the second lens. The distance between the lenses is $40 \text{ cm}$.

Object distance for the second lens, $u_2 = -(40 - 30) = -10 \text{ cm}$

For the second lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow v_2 = 10 \text{ cm}$

Since $v_2$ is positive, the final image is real.

Magnification of the second lens, $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{10}{-10} = -1$

Total magnification, $m = m_1 \times m_2 = (-2) \times (-1) = 2$

Since the total magnification is positive, the final image is erect with respect to the original object.

Thus, the final image is erect and real.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$, a $5 \text{ mm}$ high pin is placed. A second lens of focal length $5 \text{ cm}$ is located $40 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens and $55 \text{ cm}$ from the pin. Calculate the size of the final image.
questions.solution:
For the first lens, using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

Given $u_1 = -15 \text{ cm}$ and $f_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$

$v_1 = +30 \text{ cm}$

Magnification of the first lens, $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2$

For the second lens, the image formed by the first lens acts as the object. The distance between the lenses is $40 \text{ cm}$.

Object distance for the second lens, $u_2 = -(40 - 30) = -10 \text{ cm}$.

Given $f_2 = +5 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$v_2 = +10 \text{ cm}$

Magnification of the second lens, $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{10}{-10} = -1$

Total magnification of the combination is $m = m_1 \times m_2 = (-2) \times (-1) = 2$.

The size of the final image is $h_i = |m| \times h_o = 2 \times 5 \text{ mm} = 10 \text{ mm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point object is positioned at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens. The image forms on the opposite side at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens. When a concave lens is placed in contact with the convex lens, the image shifts further away by $30 \text{ cm}$. Determine the focal lengths of the two lenses.
options: $10 \text{ cm}$ for the convex lens and $30 \text{ cm}$ for the concave lens
$15 \text{ cm}$ for the convex lens and $45 \text{ cm}$ for the concave lens
$15 \text{ cm}$ for the convex lens and $60 \text{ cm}$ for the concave lens
$10 \text{ cm}$ for the convex lens and $60 \text{ cm}$ for the concave lens
questions.solution:
For the convex lens, the object distance is $u = -15 \text{ cm}$ and the image distance is $v = +30 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$:

$\dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{3}{30} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$f_1 = 10 \text{ cm}$

When the concave lens is placed in contact, the image shifts further away by $30 \text{ cm}$. The new image distance is $v' = 30 + 30 = +60 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula for the combination:

$\dfrac{1}{v'} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F}$

$\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{F}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{60} + \dfrac{4}{60} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$F = 12 \text{ cm}$

The equivalent focal length of two thin lenses in contact is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{5 - 6}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$

$f_2 = -60 \text{ cm}$

The focal length of the convex lens is $10 \text{ cm}$ and the focal length of the concave lens is $60 \text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two convex lenses, each having a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$, are positioned at a separation of $15 \text{ cm}$ with their principal axes coinciding. What happens to a light beam coming parallel to the principal axis as it exits the lens system?
options: It diverges as it comes out of the lens system.
It converges to a point exactly halfway between the lenses.
It emerges completely parallel to the principal axis.
It converges as it comes out of the lens system.
questions.solution:
For the first convex lens, the incident light beam is parallel to the principal axis. Therefore, the image is formed at its focal point.

Using the lens formula for the first lens:
$u_1 = -\infty$
$f_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$

This real image formed by the first lens acts as an object for the second lens. Since the distance between the lenses is $15 \text{ cm}$, the object distance for the second lens is:
$u_2 = -(15 \text{ cm} - 10 \text{ cm}) = -5 \text{ cm}$

Now, applying the lens formula for the second lens:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

Substitute $u_2 = -5 \text{ cm}$ and $f_2 = +10 \text{ cm}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-5} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{5} = -\dfrac{1}{10}$

$\Rightarrow v_2 = -10 \text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the final image is virtual and is formed $10 \text{ cm}$ in front of the second lens. Since the rays appear to originate from a virtual point before the second lens, the light beam diverges as it exits the lens system.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two convex lenses, each having a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$, are positioned at a separation of $15 \text{ cm}$ with their principal axes coinciding. Determine the location of the virtual image produced by the lens system for an object located far away.
options: $15 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens towards the second lens
$10 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens towards the second lens
$5 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens away from the second lens
$5 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens towards the second lens
questions.solution:
For the first lens, the object is at infinity, so $u_1 = -\infty$ and $f_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-\infty} = \dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow v_1 = +10 \text{ cm}$

The image formed by the first lens acts as a real object for the second lens. Since the distance between the two lenses is $15 \text{ cm}$, the object distance for the second lens is:

$u_2 = -(15 - 10) = -5 \text{ cm}$

For the second lens, $f_2 = +10 \text{ cm}$. Applying the lens formula again:

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-5} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{5} = -\dfrac{1}{10}$

$v_2 = -10 \text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates that the final virtual image is formed $10 \text{ cm}$ in front of the second lens.

The distance of this image from the first lens is $15 \text{ cm} - 10 \text{ cm} = 5 \text{ cm}$. Thus, the final image is located $5 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens towards the second lens.

questions.q: Two convex lenses, each having a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$, are positioned at a separation of $15 \text{ cm}$ with their principal axes coinciding. Compute the focal length of the equivalent lens. (Note that the sign of the focal length is positive even though the lens system actually diverges a parallel beam incident on it.)
questions.solution:
Given $f_1 = 10 \text{ cm}$, $f_2 = 10 \text{ cm}$, and the distance between the lenses $d = 15 \text{ cm}$.

The equivalent focal length $F$ of two thin lenses separated by a distance $d$ is given by the formula:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2} - \dfrac{d}{f_1 f_2}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{15}{10 \times 10}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{2}{10} - \dfrac{15}{100}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{20}{100} - \dfrac{15}{100}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{5}{100} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$F = 20 \text{ cm}$

questions.q: A ball is held at a height $h$ above the surface of a heavy transparent sphere having a refractive index $\mu$. The radius of the sphere is $R$. At $t = 0$, the ball is released to fall normally onto the sphere. Determine the speed of the image formed as a function of time for $t < \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$. Consider only the image produced by a single refraction.
questions.solution:
The distance of the ball from the pole of the spherical surface at time $t$ is given by $y = h - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$.

Using the sign convention, the object distance is $u = -y = - \left(h - $\dfrac{1}{2}$gt^2\right)$.

The velocity of the object is $v_o = $\dfrac{du}{dt} =$gt$.

The formula for refraction at a single spherical surface is:

\dfrac{\mu_2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_1}{u} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}

Substituting $\mu_1 = 1$ and $\mu_2 = \mu$, we get:

\dfrac{\mu}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}

Differentiating this equation with respect to time $t$ yields:

-\dfrac{\mu}{v^2} \dfrac{dv}{dt} + \dfrac{1}{u^2} \dfrac{du}{dt} =$0$

\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{v^2}{\mu u^2} \dfrac{du}{dt}

From the refraction formula, we can find the ratio \dfrac{v}{u}:

\dfrac{\mu}{v} = \dfrac{R + u(\mu - 1)}{u R}

\dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{\mu R}{R + u(\mu - 1)}

Squaring this ratio and dividing by $\mu$ gives:

\dfrac{v^2}{\mu u^2} = \dfrac{\mu R^2}{[R + u(\mu - 1)]^2}

Substituting $u = - \left(h - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\right)$ into the denominator:

$R + u(\mu - 1) = R - (\mu - 1) \left(h - $\dfrac{1}{2}$gt^2\right)$

Since this term is squared, we can reverse the sign inside the bracket:

$[R + u(\mu - 1)]^2 = \left[(\mu - 1)\left(h - $\dfrac{1}{2}$gt^2\right) - R\right]^2$

The speed of the image is the magnitude of \dfrac{dv}{dt}:

$v_i = $\dfrac{\mu R^2}{\left[(\mu - 1)\left(h - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\right) - R\right]^2} ($gt)$

$v_i = \dfrac{\mu R^2 gt}{\left[(\mu - 1)\left(h - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2\right) - R\right]^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle travels at a constant speed $V$ from a large distance towards a concave mirror of radius $R$, moving along the mirror's principal axis. Determine the speed of the image formed by the mirror as a function of the particle's distance $x$ from the mirror.
questions.solution:
The mirror formula is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$-\dfrac{1}{v^2} \dfrac{dv}{dt} - \dfrac{1}{u^2} \dfrac{du}{dt} = 0$

$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -\left(\dfrac{v}{u}\right)^2 \dfrac{du}{dt}$

The speed of the object is $V$, so \left|\dfrac{du}{dt}\right| = V$. The speed of the image is given by $v_i = \left|\dfrac{dv}{dt}\right| = m^2 V$, where $m = -\dfrac{v}{u}$ is the transverse magnification.

From the mirror formula, the magnification can be expressed as:

$m = \dfrac{f}{f - u}$

For a concave mirror, the focal length is $f = -\dfrac{R}{2}$ and the object distance is $u = -x$. Substituting these values:

$m = \dfrac{-\dfrac{R}{2}}{-\dfrac{R}{2} - (-x)} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{R}{2}}{x - \dfrac{R}{2}} = \dfrac{-R}{2x - R}$

Therefore, the speed of the image is:

$v_i = m^2 V = \left(\dfrac{-R}{2x - R}\right)^2 V = \dfrac{R^2 V}{(2x - R)^2}

The mirror together with its stand has a mass $m$. The block is pushed at $t = 0$ towards the mirror so that it starts moving towards the mirror at a constant speed $V$ and collides with it. The collision is perfectly elastic. Find the velocity of the image (a) at a time $t < d/V$, (b) at a time $t > d/V$.
questions.solution:
(a) $\dfrac{R^2 V}{[2(d - Vt) - R]^2}$
(b) $V \left(1 - $\dfrac{R^2}{[2Vt - d - R]^2}\right)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gun of mass $M$ fires a bullet of mass $m$ with a horizontal speed $V$. The gun is equipped with a concave mirror of focal length $f$ facing towards the receding bullet. Determine the speed of separation of the bullet and the image immediately after the gun is fired.
questions.solution:
Let the velocity of the bullet with respect to the ground be $V$ in the forward direction.

By the principle of conservation of linear momentum, the recoil velocity of the gun (and the mirror) is:
$v_{g} = \dfrac{m}{M}V$ (in the backward direction)

The velocity of the bullet with respect to the mirror (gun) is:
$v_{O/M} = V - (-v_{g}) = V + \dfrac{m}{M}V = V \left($1 + $\dfrac{m}{M}\right)

For a spherical mirror, the velocity of the image with respect to the mirror is given by:
$\vec{v}_{I/M} = -m_{t}^2 \vec{v}_{O/M}$
where $m_{t} = $\dfrac{f}{f - u} is the transverse magnification.

Immediately after the gun is fired, the bullet is at the pole of the mirror, so the object distance $u = 0$.
Thus, the magnification is:
$m_{t} = $\dfrac{f}{f - 0} =$1$

Substituting this into the velocity equation, we get:
$\vec{v}_{I/M} = -(1)^2 \vec{v}_{O/M} = -\vec{v}_{O/M}$

This means the image moves with the same speed as the bullet relative to the mirror, but in the exact opposite direction.

The velocity of the bullet with respect to the image is:
$\vec{v}_{B/I} = \vec{v}_{O/M} - \vec{v}_{I/M} = \vec{v}_{O/M} - (-\vec{v}_{O/M}) = 2\vec{v}_{O/M}$

Therefore, the speed of separation of the bullet and the image is:
$v_{sep} = 2v_{O/M} = 2V \left(1 + \dfrac{m}{M}\right)$

Answer: $2\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{M}\right)V$

questions.q: A mass $m = 50 \text{ g}$ is released from a height $h = 10 \text{ cm}$ above a vertical spring having a spring constant of $500 \text{ N m}^{-1}$, as shown in the figure. Upon impact, the mass sticks to the spring and subsequently executes simple harmonic oscillations. A concave mirror with a focal length of $12 \text{ cm}$ is positioned facing the mass such that its principal axis aligns with the mass's line of motion. The pole of the mirror is fixed at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ from the uncompressed free end of the spring. Determine the length over which the image of the mass oscillates.
questions.solution:
Given mass $m = 50 \text{ g} = 0.05 \text{ kg}$, height $h = 10 \text{ cm} = 0.1 \text{ m}$, and spring constant $k = 500 \text{ N m}^{-1}$.

The velocity of the mass just before striking the spring is $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.1} = \sqrt{2} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Let the uncompressed free end of the spring be the origin. When the mass sticks to the spring, it executes simple harmonic motion (SHM).

The mean position of the oscillation is at a compression $x_0$ where the spring force balances the gravitational force:

$kx_0 = mg \Rightarrow x_0 = \dfrac{0.05 \times 10}{500} = 0.001 \text{ m} = 0.1 \text{ cm}$.

The angular frequency of the SHM is $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{500}{0.05}} = 100 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

Using the velocity-displacement relation for SHM at the uncompressed position (displacement from mean position is $x_0 = 0.1 \text{ cm}$):

$v^2 = \omega^2 (A^2 - x_0^2)$

Substituting the values in standard SI units:

$(\sqrt{2})^2 = 100^2 (A^2 - 0.001^2)$

$2 = 10000 A^2 - 0.01 \Rightarrow 10000 A^2 = 2.01 \Rightarrow A^2 = 2.01 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$.

Approximating $A^2 \approx 2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$, the amplitude is $A \approx \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-2} \text{ m} = \sqrt{2} \text{ cm}$.

The length of the oscillation path of the mass is $L_o = 2A = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828 \text{ cm}$.

The pole of the concave mirror is at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ from the uncompressed free end. The object distance of the mean position is approximately $u = -30 \text{ cm}$, and the focal length is $f = -12 \text{ cm}$.

The longitudinal magnification $m_L$ of the mirror is given by:

$m_L = \left( \dfrac{f}{u - f} \right)^2 = \left( \dfrac{-12}{-30 - (-12)} \right)^2 = \left( \dfrac{-12}{-18} \right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{9}$

The length of the image over which it oscillates is:

$L_i = m_L \times L_o = \dfrac{4}{9} \times 2\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{8 \times 1.414}{9} \approx 1.25 \text{ cm}$.

The closest provided option is $1.2 \text{ cm}$.

questions.q: Consider the situation shown in the figure. The elevator is travelling upwards with an acceleration of $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the focal length of the mirror is $12.0 \text{ cm}$. All the surfaces are smooth and the pulley is light. At $t = 0$, the mass–pulley system is released from rest (with respect to the elevator) when the distance of block $B$ from the mirror is $42.0 \text{ cm}$. Determine the distance between the image of the block $B$ and the mirror at $t = 0.200 \text{ s}$. Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
questions.solution:
In the frame of the elevator, the effective acceleration due to gravity is:

$g_{\text{eff}} = g + a = 10 + 2.00 = 12.0 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

Let $a_{\text{rel}}$ be the acceleration of the blocks relative to the elevator. Writing the equations of motion for blocks A and B:

For block A: $T = m a_{\text{rel}}$

For block B: $m g_{\text{eff}} - T = m a_{\text{rel}}$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$m g_{\text{eff}} = 2m a_{\text{rel}} \Rightarrow a_{\text{rel}} = \dfrac{g_{\text{eff}}}{2} = \dfrac{12.0}{2} = 6.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

The distance fallen by block B relative to the elevator in time $t = 0.200 \text{ s}$ is:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} a_{\text{rel}} t^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} (6.00) (0.200)^2 = 0.12 \text{ m} = 12.0 \text{ cm}$

The initial distance of block B from the mirror is $42.0 \text{ cm}$. At $t = 0.200 \text{ s}$, its distance from the mirror becomes:

$d = 42.0 - 12.0 = 30.0 \text{ cm}$

Applying the sign convention, the object distance is $u = -30.0 \text{ cm}$.

The mirror shown in the figure bulges towards the object, so it is a convex mirror. Its focal length is $f = +12.0 \text{ cm}$.

Using the mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{-30.0} = \dfrac{1}{12.0}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{12.0} + \dfrac{1}{30.0} = \dfrac{5 + 2}{60.0} = \dfrac{7}{60.0}$

$v = \dfrac{60.0}{7} \approx 8.57 \text{ cm}$

The distance between the image of block B and the mirror is $8.57 \text{ cm}$.
